newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat's office confirms resignation offers.
newsitem.headline: Arafat's office confirms resignation offers.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's office confirmed on Saturday that members of his cabinet had submitted their resignations and said he would consider the offer at a "suitable time".

"Some ministers submitted their resignations and asked Arafat to consider these resignations at a suitable time," the brief statement said. Agriculture Minister Abdel Jawad Saleh said earlier that 16 of 18 ministers had offered to quit.
The statement, issued after a four-hour cabinet meeting in the West Bank town of Ramallah, gave no other details and Arafat's office declined to elaborate.

The resignation offers followed a damning report from a panel of the Palestinian Legislative Council this week detailing alleged corruption and mismanagement of funds by the Palestinian Authority and calling for two ministers to be put on trial.
The council itself voted 56-1 on Thursday to give Arafat one month to dissolve his cabinet and replace it with "qualified and experienced ministers" after debating the report.

Arafat is already grappling with a grave crisis in his tottering peace process with Israel after a twin suicide bombing by Islamist militants in a Jerusalem market on Wednesday. The blasts killed 15 people, including the two attackers.
